newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU postpones complaint on Cuba deal.
newsitem.headline: EU postpones complaint on Cuba deal.

text.p: European Union states agreed Monday to postpone a planned complaint against the Helms-Burton Act, but left until Wednesday more considered reaction to the tentative transatlantic deal on Cuba policy.
"It is agreed that we do not put forward our case in the WTO today," EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan told a news conference after meeting with ambassadors from the 15 EU nations.

His announcement follows a deal struck between the European Commission and Washington Friday to defuse a festering battle over the Helms-Burton legislation, which aims to isolate the government of Fidel Castro by discouraging foreign investment in Cuba.
The Europeans have been threatening high-profile action at the Geneva-based World Trade Organisation in retaliation for the U.S. law.
Brittan said the ambassadors would meet again Wednesday to decide formally whether to suspend the EU's complaint.

A Spanish diplomat said several ambassadors had urged Monday that the EU hold a strong line against Washington's tendency to enact domestic laws against countries such as Iran, Cuba and Libya without thought to the extra-territorial effects of those laws.

The diplomat said Spain, along with Belgium, France and Italy, agreed that Wednesday's meeting should prepare a supplementary EU declaration to the deal covering both Helms-Burton and the U.S. Iran-Libya Sanctions Act.
"The EU does not accept extra-territorial legislation. That's something which is not clear in the understanding agreed between with the United States," the diplomat said.
